name: Juan March Delgado
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Juan March Delgado is one of the two largest shareholders of $2.5 billion (net assets) Banca March, Spain's only 100% family-owned bank.
Juan and his billionaire brother Carlos March Delgado are grandchildren of Banca March's founder, Juan March (d. 1962), who started the business in Palma de Mallorca in 1926.
Until 2018, Juan was co-chairman of the $5 billion (net assets) investment company Corporación Financiera Alba, which is also nearly 100% family-owned.
Juan and Carlos March Delgado own 69% of Banca March and 42% of Corporación Financiera Alba combined (excluding Banca March's 15% stake in Corporación Financiera Alba).
Juan is president of the family's philanthropic foundation, Fundación Juan March, which focuses on the arts.

name: Daniel Pritzker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Daniel Pritzker is one of 13 billionaire heirs in the Chicago-based Pritzker family, whose best known creation is Hyatt Hotels.
A filmmaker, in 2019 Pritzker released Bolden, a biographical drama about New Orleans trumpeter Buddy Bolden, after over a decade working on it.
He made a silent film, Louis, about the life of Louis Armstrong, which was released to critical praise in 2010.
Daniel's brother Tom is the chairman of Hyatt Hotels; his sister Gigi is a film producer.
Daniel's charitable foundation, named after his father and Hyatt founder Jay Pritzker, pledged $100 million to California community colleges in 2020.
forbes_facts: Pritzker used to own Jerry Garcia's guitar; he auctioned it and donated the proceeds, $3.2 million, to the Southern Poverty Law Center.
Pritzker is also a guitarist and the primary songwriter for Sonia Dada, a fusion rock and soul band.

name: Gudrun Heine
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Gudrun Heine's father founded Karl Storz SE & Co. KG in 1945 to manufacture ENT (Ear, Nose & Throat) instruments, headlamps and binocular loupes.
Karl Storz pioneered the idea of introducing into the body (via a flexible fiber-optic cable) bright light generated by an external source.
This "cold light illumination" innovation paved the way for modern endoscopy and laid the foundation for the company's future success.
Today, with a portfolio of 15,000+ products, Storz is a leader in endoscopy instruments for human and veterinary medicine as well as industrial use.
Heine holds 44% of the privately owned company, which is based in Tuttlingen, Germany.
forbes_facts: Her sister, Sybill, who also owns 44%, stepped down as managing director on January 1, 2019 and handed over the reins to her son Karl-Christian.

name: Huang Xiaofen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2019-2020)

Her husband, Liu Shaobo, heads the company. He previously worked for a state-owned company in Shenzhen early in his career.
Kinwong grew out of a joint venture backed by that government business.

name: Greg Mondre
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Greg Mondre is co-CEO of Silver Lake, a private equity firm specializing in making technology investments.
Silver Lake is based in Silicon Valley and oversees about $100 billion.
Mondre joined Silver Lake in 1999 after stints at Goldman Sachs and private equity firm TPG.
Mondre has worked on deals for  Motorola Solutions, Red Ventures, WP Engine, GoodRx and GoDaddy.

name: Manuel Villar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Manuel Villar is the chairman of property developer Vista Land & Lifescapes run by his son Manuel Paolo.

Villar's biggest asset is his stake in Villar Land Holdings (formerly Golden MV Holdings), a property developer which is building Villar City, a 3,500-hectare master-planned community south of Manila.
He also has five other listed entities including mall operator Vistamalls, property landlord VistaREIT, home improvement chain AllHome, supermarket chain AllDay Marts and Premiere Island Power REIT.
Villar is diversifying his business with new investments in free-to-air TV and plans to build a casino and a theme park in southern Metro Manila.
His son Mark and daughter Camille are senators in the Philippines.
forbes_facts: Villar has been involved in politics and held positions including congressman, speaker of the house of representatives, senator and senate president.
As a child, Villar helped his mother sell seafood in a Manila market.

name: Ramesh Jaisinghani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Ramesh Jaisinghani gets his fortune from his stake in Polycab India, which makes electrical wires and cables.
Polycab was started by his older brother Inder  as a trading firm in 1986.
It supplies everything from power cables to solar cables to optical fibre cables to the power, oil and gas and renewable energy industries.
In 2014, Polycab expanded into making products such as electric fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear. It went public in 2019.
His son Nikhil Jaisinghani sits on the board of Polycab.

name: Li Jianquan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Li Jianquan chairs Winner Medical, a supplier of disposable wound care and surgical products.
Winner, which began manufacturing cotton-based medical dressings in 1991, went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in September 2020.
The company also makes protective face masks and surgical gowns, as well as bandages and gauze products.
Winner products are sold at more than 40,000 pharmacies across China and in more than 70 countries.

name: Antonio Marcegaglia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Antonio Marcegaglia is the CEO and chairman of Marcegaglia, one of Italy's largest steel manufacturers and the world's largest maker of welded tubes.
He owns half of the company, with the other half owned by his sister Emma; the siblings took over after the death of their father Steno in 2013.
Steno founded the company in 1959 in the northern Italian city of Mantua and grew it into a multinational firm with operations on multiple continents.
Marcegaglia processes 6.2 million tons of steel a year and posted $6.6 billion in sales in 2019.
